name: Electromagnet module (KS0320, P20/15 magnet)
description: 5 V holding electromagnet (20 mm x 15 mm P20/15 type, sold as KK-P20/15 or ZYE1-P20/15) on a small board with an on-board SOT-23 transistor switch and a flyback diode across the coil. The coil runs from the 5 V VCC pin; the SIG pin only switches the transistor, so a 3.3 V GPIO can drive it. SIG high = magnet on (holds about 1 kg of iron), low = off; PWM on SIG weakens the pull. Sold as: Keyestudio Electromagnet Module KS0320 (black board), 4-pin header GND, VCC, NC, SIG.
eli5: A coil around an iron core that becomes a magnet only while switched on: set the pin high and it grabs a steel screw, set it low and the screw drops.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Coil supply, 5 V at up to about 0.3-0.4 A (connect to the board's 5 V / VBUS pin, never 3.3 V)

pins.name: NC
pins.description: Not connected on the board; leave it unwired

pins.name: SIG
pins.description: Control input: high = magnet on, low = off; PWM (e.g. 1 kHz) sets the holding strength. Only drives the on-board transistor, so a 3.3 V GPIO is enough.

buildNotes: Wire VCC to 5 V (ESP32 VIN/5V, Pico VBUS), GND to GND and SIG to any GPIO; leave NC unconnected. The coil current comes from VCC through the on-board transistor, never from the GPIO.

The coil draws roughly 0.3-0.4 A at 5 V (Keyestudio: 0.3 A max, 3 W max; Seeed's module with the same P20/15 magnet: 400 mA). A USB port can supply that, but power several magnets or motors from a separate 5 V supply with a shared ground.
High = hold, low = release. PWM on SIG (machine.PWM, about 1 kHz) reduces the holding force; a brief full-on pulse then a lower duty saves power and heat once the object is held.
The coil gets warm if left on for long periods. Switch it off when not holding something.

The magnet holds best on flat, clean iron or steel at least 5 mm thick (P20/15 datasheet: 25 N rated holding force, about 1 kg in practice). Thin sheet, aluminium, brass and stainless steel hold weakly or not at all.
The on-board flyback diode across the coil absorbs the voltage spike at switch-off, so no extra diode is needed. Do not wire a bare electromagnet coil straight to a GPIO.

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import time

magnet = Pin({SIG}, Pin.OUT, value=0)  # SIG high = magnet on
while True:
    magnet.value(1)
    print('MAGNET ON')
    time.sleep(2)
    magnet.value(0)
    print('MAGNET OFF')
    time.sleep(2)

test.title: The electromagnet switches on, then off again
